title: Anticipatory scheduler bug causing reserved-pool underprovisioning during rapid ramp
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers experienced degraded throughput and elevated latency when their dedicated reserved pools failed to scale quickly during short, steep traffic ramps. The autoscaler’s anticipatory scheduling component under-provisioned headroom because it used a conservative smoothing and a flawed burst-credit accounting path that reported more available burst headroom than actually present across zonal segments.

Root cause: Two interacting defects: (1) The predictive estimator used a 60s median-based smoothing window that suppressed short high-slope ramps; it reported lower expected qps so the scheduler didn’t allocate burst nodes. (2) Cross-zone burst accounting aggregated per-zone credits using a stale cache key, causing double-counting for tenants with active multi-zone allocations; the controller believed there was spare burst capacity and deferred scale-ups. Together these caused silent underprovisioning during ramp events.

Impact: Intermittent customer-facing request queueing and token-level timeouts; most visible for customers with bursty workloads and pinned reserved pools. Several high-traffic customers reported request latency > 3x SLO for 3-9 minute windows and escalated to support.

Mitigation applied (hotfix): Deployed a rollback of the stale cache path (hotfix 1) to stop double-counting (short-term mitigation), and increased autoscaler safe-headroom floor to force immediate emergency scale-up while we validate estimator changes (hotfix 2). These mitigations reduced customer impact within 6 minutes of activation.

Planned permanent fix: 1) Replace median smoothing with an exp-weighted moving average that preserves short slope events plus a configurable peak-shift multiplier for tenants marked as bursty. 2) Rework cross-zone burst-credit reconciliation to use authoritative lease-backed accounting and remove stale cache precedence. 3) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate multi-zone burst ramps and assert no underprovisioning. 4) Add telemetry: per-tenant predicted_qps, estimator_confidence, and burst-credit-freshness metrics.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for estimator logic and credit accounting land in PR; integration tests will run in a dedicated e2e cluster that imitates multi-zone behaviour. Canary rollout plan: canary to 2 non-prod regions -> 1 production region with 5% of traffic -> full roll after 48h of stable metrics.

Monitoring & alerts: New alerts created for estimator_confidence < 0.2 and burst_credit_staleness > 30s. Dashboards updated for predicted vs observed qps, per-tenant reconciliation failures, and scale latency percentiles.

Customer communications: Support notified impacted customers with post-incident summary and temporary mitigation steps. We will send a follow-up with permanent-fix ETA and invite impacted customers to a technical sync.

Deliverables: PRs (estimator, accounting), e2e test harness, runbook update, customer comms draft, postmortem.
